title: Account Enumeration via Error-Based Detection
description:
The registration endpoint (/api/register.php) reveals whether usernames and emails already exist in the system through different HTTP response codes. When a user attempts to register with a username or email that already exists, the server returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. When registering with new, unique credentials, the server returns HTTP 200 with a success message. This response code differentiation allows attackers to systematically enumerate valid usernames and email addresses without needing to access the database directly.

Additionally, the application uses case-insensitive username matching, meaning variations like "enumtest1" and "ENUMTEST1" are treated as duplicates, further enabling enumeration through case manipulation attempts.

The vulnerability stems from improper error handling that exposes account existence information through HTTP status codes rather than using generic responses for all registration attempts.
impact:
Attackers can systematically enumerate valid user accounts in the system by observing HTTP response codes. This information can be leveraged for:
- Targeted social engineering attacks against known users
- Account takeover attempts using enumerated usernames
- Identifying administrative or high-value accounts
- Combined with weak password policies (as identified in separate findings), enabling targeted brute force attacks
- Building a comprehensive user database for the organization

The enumeration process can be automated and scaled to identify a large portion of the user base with minimal detection risk.
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability:

Test Results:
- New Account Registration (unique): HTTP 200 - {\"success\":true,\"message\":\"Registration successful.\"}
- Duplicate Username: HTTP 500 - Empty body
- Duplicate Email: HTTP 500 - Empty body  
- Case Variation of Existing Username: HTTP 500 - Empty body

The POC demonstrates reliable account enumeration by analyzing response codes:
- HTTP 200 indicates a successful new registration
- HTTP 500 indicates the username or email already exists
- Case-insensitive matching means variations of usernames return 500, confirming existence

Example commands executed:
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/register.php -d 'username=enumtest_1234567890&password=test123&email=enumtest_1234567890@test.com'
# Returns: HTTP 200 (New account created)

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/register.php -d 'username=enumtest_1234567890&password=different&email=different@test.com'
# Returns: HTTP 500 (Username exists)

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/register.php -d 'username=ENUMTEST_1234567890&password=test123&email=casetest@test.com'
# Returns: HTTP 500 (Case variation matches existing user)
```
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor, CWE-204: Response Timing Side Channel, OWASP User Enumeration
toolCallDescription: Documenting confirmed account enumeration vulnerability with working POC
